bench.notes: The bench top: page ground, summary box, hovered frame, current-plan row, disabled button, inline-code ground. Lower of the two material levels; the panel sits 1.28:1 above it in both themes.

panel.contrast: ink on panel 17.89:1 light / 12.44:1 dark; ink-2 on panel 6.32:1 light / 5.90:1 dark
panel.notes: The lit reading surface. Carries the note body, the roll, sheets, compare panes, the auth slate, pager cells and default buttons.

well.notes: A recess cut into the material, dark in BOTH themes: header rail, counter plates, gate head, progress and quota troughs, table header rows, active pager cell, slate plate and clapper, code blocks. This is the machine, not a surface.

perf.notes: The colour seen through a sprocket hole. Matches the bench in light; deliberately lighter than the well in dark so holes read as punched rather than as black-on-black.

ink.notes: Primary type and the hover border for default buttons and inputs.

ink-2.contrast: 6.32:1 on panel and 5.36:1 on tape in light; 5.90:1 and 4.79:1 in dark
ink-2.notes: Secondary type: summaries, hints, labels, edge codes, metadata, prose bullets, ghost button.

on-film.notes: Type and marks on dark material. Does NOT invert between themes; also the quota fill and the gate marker.

edge.notes: The 1px rule drawn ON the light box: panel-level dividers, frame separators, heading underlines, table cells.

edge-2.notes: The 1px rule drawn ON the bench: outer container borders, form controls, dashed placement zones, footer rule.

wax-red.notes: Grease pencil, text weight. Means cut / destroy / required: delete button, error lists, required marker, hovered edge-code ID, hovered file-drop dashes.

wax-red-fill.notes: The same pencil pressed down. The most-used token in the stylesheet (17 uses): every wax rule under a title, primary button, file-selector button, active tape, plan badge, the advance bar, trim-bin hang marks, frame registration corner-marks, the streaming caret.

wax-blue.notes: Means splice. Links, backlink splice marks, input focus border, the global focus-visible outline, the ok notice. Never a primary action, never a surface fill.

wax-amber.notes: DECLARED AND THEME-MAPPED BUT NOT APPLIED anywhere in the current build. Reserved for amber type on a light surface; any future use is still bound to the warning-only job.

wax-amber-fill.notes: Means be careful. Ships on exactly one component: the warning notice. Identical in both themes.

on-fill.notes: Type on a red fill. Does not invert between themes.

on-warn.notes: Near-black on the amber fill. Deliberately does NOT invert between themes; the pigment is opaque and does not follow the room light.

ctr-hot.notes: The only variant colour a counter may take: figures recolour to this when a quota reaches 80%. Sits on the well plate, which is dark in both themes, so it does not invert.

tape.notes: Tape stock, a separate material from the panel. Used only as the tag chip's ground, shaped by the tape mask, and the chip carries no border at all.

display.purpose: Page title and note title. Always followed by a red wax rule. Drops to 1.55rem below 620px.

headline.purpose: Sheet headings, prose h1/h2, the slate form title. Carries a 1px edge rule beneath.

title.purpose: Roll frame titles, prose h3, compare-pane titles.

body.purpose: Note prose and general copy. Capped at 74ch.

small.purpose: Summaries, buttons, field captions, table cells, gate output.

fine.purpose: Hints, tags, trim-bin items, margin-column lists.

label.purpose: Machine markings: rail switches, section labels, table headers, footer, badges. Width 84, uppercase, 0.14em (0.10-0.12em inside tighter components).

counter.purpose: Every quantity the user compares or watches. Width 116, tabular. Always rendered through the .ctr plate component.

mono.purpose: Textarea input and code only. The only non-Archivo face in the system.

fonts.loading: font-display: swap; the latin file is preloaded in the head
fonts.note: CJK deliberately falls through to the system gothic stack (Hiragino Kaku Gothic ProN, Yu Gothic, Noto Sans JP, PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei). A CJK webfont would be multiple megabytes and would damage the 20-35s ingest wait screen the product is built around. Widths actually used are 84-116; the axis extremes 62 and 125 are never taken.

masks.name: wax-mask
masks.purpose: Hand-authored grease-pencil stroke, tiled at 60px, applied as a CSS mask so the shape comes from the asset and the colour still comes from a token. Draws every red rule in the product.

masks.name: tape-mask
masks.purpose: Hand-authored torn-tape outline. Shapes the .tape chip via a ::before at z-index -1; the chip has no border at all.

extensions.shadowPolicy: There are no box-shadows anywhere in the stylesheet, in either theme. Depth is made only by a 1px rule (edge on the light box, edge-2 on the bench) plus the bench-to-panel material step, measured at 1.28:1 in light and 1.28:1 in dark - deliberately matched so the raise reads identically in both rooms. Do not add a shadow, glow, gradient fill or backdrop blur.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Background, colour and border-colour transitions on buttons and rail switches.

motion.name: hover-fast
motion.purpose: Roll frame background and the fade-in of the red registration corner-marks.

motion.name: advance
motion.purpose: The ingest advance bar width and the gate marker position. Linear is required, not a default: an eased progress bar reads as decelerating when the real process is not.

motion.name: measure
motion.purpose: The quota fill. Eased on purpose - it is a standing measurement, not a live process.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: The blinking wax-red block caret on the streaming gate output. Stops when the stream completes.

motion.name: hang
motion.purpose: Trim-bin items settling onto their pin, staggered 40ms per item up to 600ms.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Stops the advance transition, the gate marker, the quota fill, the caret blink and the trim-bin hang. Deliberately KEEPS colour and border transitions - removing those would remove the only cue for where the pointer is.

breakpoints.name: collapse
breakpoints.purpose: Note layout and A/B compare drop to one column; the margin column reflows below the light box as an auto-fit grid of minmax(180px, 1fr) blocks with its dividing rules removed.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes static (it wraps to three rows and would otherwise take a third of the viewport), search takes a full row, icon-only switches reveal their labels, display type drops to 1.55rem, roll frames drop the edge-code column.

invariants: border-radius does not appear in the stylesheet. Radius is 0 everywhere, no exceptions.
box-shadow does not appear in the stylesheet. Depth is a 1px rule plus the panel/bench material step, full stop.
The bench-to-panel material step is 1.28:1 in both light and dark, matched deliberately.
The rail, counter plates, gate head, progress troughs, table headers and slate plate are dark in both themes.
--on-warn, --on-fill, --on-film and --ctr-hot have no dark-theme override; wax is opaque pigment.
The progress meter never goes backwards and never overshoots the next real checkpoint (public/js/app.js, Meter.set and Meter.tick).
Red cuts, blue splices, amber warns. No colour takes another colour's job.

narrative.overview:
GridMind's product value is subtraction — it deletes everything in a document that is not knowledge — so its interface is a film editor's cutting bench, not a dashboard. The whole world is built from one physical fiction: material runs through a machine, the machine throws most of it away, and what survives is laid on a light box to be read. Every surface in the build answers to that fiction. The page ground is bench grey. The rail across the top is the machine: always dark, in both themes, because a machine is not paper and does not change colour when the room lights come on. The note list is not a card grid; it is one continuous strip of film with an unbroken sprocket column down its left edge and frames divided by hairlines. Numbers are footage counters — dark recessed plates with expanded tabular figures. Marks are grease pencil in three colours that each have exactly one job.

The system is aggressively flat and aggressively square. There is no border radius anywhere and no box-shadow anywhere; those are not defaults that happened, they are the two hardest invariants in the file. Depth is made only two ways: a 1px rule, and a material step between the bench and the panel. That step is measured at 1.28:1 in light and 1.28:1 in dark — deliberately matched, so the bench and the light box sit the same distance apart in both rooms. The result is dense, tool-like, and quiet: pure geometry, one accent that means "cut", and a lot of restraint about where light is allowed.

It refuses the arrangement its category ships. There is no left sidebar, no card grid, no rounded surface floating on a soft shadow, no pastel status pill. What it also refuses is decoration for its own sake — the world's devices (sprockets, counters, wax rules, tape, the clapper stripe) are structural, they mark where the machine touched the material, and none of them is applied twice for effect. The clapper stripe appears on the auth slate and nowhere else.
keyCharacteristics: Bench-grey ground, one lit panel; zero radius, zero shadow
Depth from a 1px rule plus a 1.28:1 material step, matched in both themes
An always-dark machine rail, identical in light and dark
Sprocket perforations as the structural signature, not as ornament
Footage counters: dark plates, expanded tabular Archivo, one component for every number
Three grease-pencil colours with fixed, non-overlapping jobs
Hand-authored SVG applied as CSS masks so shape comes from the asset and colour from a token
Hand-drawn single-weight SVG icon sprite; no icon font, no emoji

rules.name: The Three Pencils Rule
rules.body: Red cuts, blue splices, amber warns. A colour never takes another colour's job. Red is the only colour a primary action may use; blue is the only colour a link or focus ring may use; amber appears on warnings only, and today on exactly one component. Two review rounds were spent enforcing this after earlier drafts let red and blue drift into decoration — if a new surface needs a fourth meaning, it gets a shape or a rule, not a fourth pigment.

rules.name: The Opaque Pigment Rule
rules.body: --on-warn, --on-fill, --on-film and --ctr-hot do not invert between themes, and --wax-amber-fill and --wax-red-fill keep their dark-mode-adjacent values. Wax is opaque pigment on physical material; it does not change because the room lights changed. Never add a dark-theme override for an on-* token.

rules.name: The One Lit Surface Rule
rules.body: On any reading surface, exactly one panel glows and the bench does not. On the note detail view this is literal — the light box is the only lit thing on the page, the margin column sits directly on the bench with no surface of its own.

rules.name: The Width-Is-Role Rule
rules.body: Role is expressed by font-variation-settings: 'wdth', not by adding a family. 84 = machine marking, 88-96 = heading, 100 = prose, 116 = counter. A new role picks a width on that scale; it does not introduce a second typeface.

rules.name: The One Counter Rule
rules.body: Every quantity the user compares — quota, percent complete, character counts, note totals, the cut ratio — goes through the .ctr component so that they are all the same object. A number typeset as plain prose is a defect, not a variant.

rules.name: The No-Webfont-For-CJK Rule
rules.body: Latin is self-hosted; CJK falls through to the system stack, permanently. The wait screen is the product's signature surface and must not carry a multi-megabyte font download.

rules.name: The Rule-And-Step Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to separate from what is behind it, give it a 1px rule in the correct edge token and, if it is a reading surface, the panel material. Never a shadow, never a glow, never a gradient, never a blur.

rules.name: The Dark Machine Rule
rules.body: Machine parts — the rail, counter plates, gate head, progress troughs, table header rows, the slate plate — use the well and on-film tokens in both themes. They are not surfaces that respond to the room; they are the equipment.

dos: Do put every number through the counter component (.ctr, wdth 116, tabular) so quota, percent, character counts and totals are recognisably the same object.
Do express a new role with Archivo's width axis (84 marking / 88-96 heading / 100 prose / 116 counter) rather than by adding a typeface.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px rule plus the panel/bench material step — edge for rules on the light box, edge-2 for rules on the bench.
Do keep the machine dark in both themes: rail, counter plates, gate head, progress troughs, table headers, the slate plate.
Do draw every red rule with the wax mask asset at 60px tiling, so all of them share one hand.
Do use linear timing on any bar reporting real elapsed time, and reserve ease for standing measurements.
Do give any new world device a job — a sprocket, a counter, a wax rule, or a tape must mark something real, or it does not go on the page.
Do ship icons from the hand-drawn sprite in views/partials/header.ejs at 1.6 stroke, square caps, miter joins, 17px.
donts: Don't add a border-radius. Anywhere. The system has one shape token and its value is 0.
Don't add a box-shadow, glow, gradient fill, or backdrop blur. There are none in the build and depth must not be made this way.
Don't let a wax colour take another wax colour's job — no blue primary buttons, no red links, no amber outside a warning.
Don't add a dark-theme override for --on-warn, --on-fill, --on-film or --ctr-hot; wax is opaque pigment and does not follow the room light.
Don't mark the current/hovered item with a left accent bar; this world uses registration corner-marks.
Don't rebuild the note list as cards, or reintroduce a sidebar; the roll is one continuous strip and the navigation is the rail.
Don't reuse the clapper stripe outside the auth slate, and don't add a second full-width red bar to a page that already has one under its title.
Don't add a CJK webfont; the system stack is the permanent answer, for the sake of the ingest wait screen.
Don't use round list bullets in prose; the bullet is a 7px square sprocket hole.
Don't use emoji or an icon font. Extend the SVG sprite instead.
openItems: The counter disappears on the slate plate. .ctr sets its own well background, but .slate-plate is also well, so the LOGIN counter on the auth nameplate loses its plate and reads as plain type rather than as a counter. The counter component needs a variant (or a border/inset treatment) for use on well-coloured ground. Do not solve it by removing the counter.

Three surfaces carry no world device. Sprockets appear on the roll, the gate, the quota bar and the auth slate. The note form, the import form and the settings language panel are plain bordered sheets and read as ordinary forms — the world stops at their edge.

The type never reaches the scale the world allows. Archivo's width extremes (62 and 125) are never taken; the used range is 84-116. --t-display caps at 1.9rem. The world's material would support a much louder display setting than the build takes.

Two declared colour tokens are unused. --wax-amber (amber text) and --on-blue (type on a blue fill) are defined and theme-mapped but applied nowhere. They are honest reservations for the roles they name, not evidence that those roles ship today.

Tape is nearly invisible on the panel. The tape token against the panel token is a very small material step in light theme, so tags inside the roll and the light box read as bare text and the torn-tape silhouette is largely lost. The device is doing its job on the bench, not on the panel.
contractDivergences: The direction contract states one lit white light-box that is the only surface allowed to glow. In the build the panel token is a general material: the roll, sheets, compare panes, the auth slate, pager cells and default buttons all use it. The rule holds literally on the note detail view and as a per-page intent everywhere else, but it is not a global invariant, so The One Lit Surface Rule is recorded scoped to reading surfaces.

The contract names amber warns as one of three equal pigments. In the build amber ships on exactly one component and its text token is unused, so the working palette is effectively two pigments plus a warning fill. The three-pencil rule still governs new work, but the shipped ratio should not be mistaken for parity.
